title: Decision-Making Language: Gerunds and Infinitives in Conversation

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I've been considering applying for the exchange programme to Vienna. But I keep putting off actually doing anything about it.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I can't decide whether to go for a semester or to stay here and finish my thesis on time. Both feel important.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Have you tried making a list of pros and cons? It sounds basic but I find it helps when I can't stop going back and forth.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I've tried doing that. The problem is that both sides feel equally compelling. Vienna would mean delaying completing the thesis.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: She says she would support me going, but she reminds me to consider the deadline implications carefully.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: That sounds like she wants you to go but doesn't want to be blamed for the delay.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Ha! Possibly. She also suggested considering whether I could do preliminary research in Vienna — which would actually contribute to the thesis.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: So going would mean combining two things instead of treating them as opposed. That changes the decision.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I know. I've been trying to avoid thinking about it that way because it makes the decision harder.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Or easier — because now you need to stop seeing them as a choice and start imagining how to do both.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: You're annoyingly right. I regret not having raised this with her earlier. I should have thought of asking sooner.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Well, you're thinking about it now. That's the point of conversations like this.

questions.text: "I've been considering applying for the programme." — "considering + applying":
opts: consider + gerund; apply = gerund object of considering
questions.correct: consider + gerund; apply = gerund object of considering
questions.hint: "consider" + GERUND. "Applying" = gerund object of "considering." "I've been considering APPLYING." ✅

questions.text: "I regret not having raised this earlier." — "not having raised" is:
questions.hint: "Not having raised" = negative perfect gerund. "Regret + gerund" for past action (or in this case, past non-action). ✅

questions.text: "She reminds me to consider the deadline implications." — "to consider" because:
questions.hint: "remind + object + TO + infinitive." "She reminds me TO CONSIDER." ✅

questions.text: "I keep putting ___ (it) off. I can't stop ___ (think) back and forth."
questions.hint: "putting it off" (phrasal verb) + "can't stop THINKING" (stop + gerund = the activity ends). ✅
